question.value: How are young star clusters spatially and temporally related to GMCs in NGC 7793, and is the cluster hierarchy inherited from the GMC hierarchy?

evidence.quote: We present an investigation of the relationship between giant molecular cloud (GMC) properties and the associated stellar clusters in the nearby flocculent galaxy NGC 7793.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2015.1.00782.S.
We observed the CO (2–1) transition with ALMA band 6 (230.36366 GHz)
We observed the CO (2–1) transition with ALMA band 6 (230.36366 GHz)
The total integration time is 3 hours with the 12-m array with 149 pointings at 72.6 seconds of integration per pointing with a mosaic spacing of 12.9$''$ between pointings.
Our angular resolution of 0.85$''$ allows us to resolve sub-GMC sizes (8 pc scales)
we are sensitive to emission on scales as large as 11” ($\sim$175 pc)

findings_qualitative.value: Clusters emerge from natal clouds much faster than cloud dispersal timescales (~10–30 Myr).

evidence.quote: Thus, star clusters are able to emerge from their natal clouds long before the timescale required for clouds to disperse.
